"When you track your basal body temperature (BBT) every day, you should eventually be able to predict roughly when you're going to ovulate. Your body temperature naturally rises throughout your cycle. It is lower in the first half (during the period and follicular phase), and then rises a tiny bit at ovulation. Once you see that rise and the temperatures stay high, you can assume that you have ovulated."

"Select or add a wearable to sync your temperature data from, or enter your temperature manually.
You’ll only see one source of data at a time. Your data will be saved if you select another source."
Throughout your cycle, your body temperature shifts slightly, and these fluctuations can tell you when you’re most fertile—right around ovulation.
Tracking your Basal Body Temperature (BBT) is a great way to either plan for pregnancy or avoid it.

In the first half of your cycle (during your period and the follicular phase), your temperature is usually lower. After ovulation, your BBT rises about 0.5°F to 1.0°F (or 0.3°C to 0.6°C). Your temperature stays elevated through the luteal phase (the second half of your cycle) and drops again just before your period starts.

"After a few months of tracking your BBT, you'll begin to see patterns that can help you anticipate ovulation (when you’re at your most fertile), since the temperature rise happens just after ovulation has occurred."

"For centuries people have tracked the movement of heavenly bodies in synchronization with our own. The word menstruation itself means moon change. And the journey of the moon exactly matches the length of a menstrual cycle. What does it all mean?
Over centuries a garden of potent symbolism has grown up around that little disc in the night sky.
William Butler Yeats considered the moon the symbol of change. Aeschylus called it the eye of the night. The Buddha achieved enlightenment on the day of the full moon. And Saint Augustine wrote that The moon is born every month, increases, is perfected, diminishes, is consumed, is renewed.
By syncing your period to the seen and unseen cosmos, you’re joining an ancient witchy history of people who celebrate the moon’s influence on terrestrial life."
"But we won't let your circle know until you decide to. For now, your cycle will show as normal, until you decide to reveal your pregnancy."
